title: Tenant Growth Accelerator — Architect-first Expansion Playbook
content:
Tenant Growth Accelerator — Architect-first Expansion Playbook

Purpose:
This playbook is a tactical, architect-focused framework for converting high-value tenants from hosted tiers into Dedicated capacity, Private deployments, or Premium SLA add-ons. It centers technical stakeholders (platform/infra/ML engineers) early in the motion to reduce friction and shorten procurement cycles.

Intended audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs) leading expansion conversations
- Solutions Engineers and Customer Architects supporting technical validation
- Sales Engineers during contract negotiation
- RevOps and legal for packaging and SOW artifacts

When to use this playbook:
- Customer shows sustained usage growth (token consumption trending > 3x baseline over 90 days)
- P95 latency or throttling incidents impacting user experience
- Security/compliance requirements that demand VPC/private deployment or dedicated tenancy
- Request for guaranteed SLA or predictable monthly capacity

Primary goals:
1) Remove technical blockers by surface-level architecture validation within 7 business days.
2) Deliver a pilot/POC that demonstrates 20–40% unit-cost improvement or measurable latency wins for core flows.
3) Achieve contract signature or pilot-to-paid handoff within 8 weeks for mid-market deals, 12 weeks for complex enterprise migrations.

Stakeholders and RACI (high level):
- CSM: owner (drive conversation, timelines, exec sponsor activation)
- Customer Architect / SE: owner (technical plan, pilot scope, acceptance criteria)
- Product (hosted/dedicated/private): consult (capacity planning, model compatibility)
- Solutions/Professional Services: support (migration runbook, on-site/remote assistance)
- Legal/RevOps: consult/approve (contracts, amendments, SOW)

QBR-style template to surface expansion signals (to use as a trigger sheet inside QBR):
- Opening executive summary (1–2 lines): usage trend + top ask
- Key metrics (last 90 days): token usage, calls/sec, P95 latency, error rate, embedding volume, cost per 1M tokens (hosted)
- Business impact: top product flows affected, user-facing symptoms, estimated revenue impact of outages/latency
- Technical health snapshot: average seq len, KV cache hit rate, concurrency peaks, model versions in use
- Opportunity hypothesis: why Dedicated/Private/SLA improves the above (latency, isolation, cost predictability)
- Proposed next steps and timeline (discovery -> pilot -> contract -> migration)
- Ask: specific value commitments (target latency, monthly committed throughput, SLA uptime %)

Renewal & migration tracker (lightweight row format — one line per customer):
- Customer | Current tier | ARR | 90d token trend (%) | Top contact (name/email) | Tech lead | Pilot window | Commit ask | Renewal date | Risk level | Next action
Example: "Acme Retail | hosted-standard | $72,000 | +210% | marta@acme.io | J. Rivera | 2026-03-15 to 2026-04-02 | 3x reserved GPUs | 2026-07-01 | medium | schedule infra review"

Playbook phases (detailed):
1) Rapid Discovery (days 0–7)
   - Deliverable: one-page tech snapshot and prioritized risk list.
   - Activities: review logs/metrics, gather model sizes & sequence length profiles, cost baseline (hosted spend per model), identify compliance (data residency/KMS) requirements.
   - Templated artifacts: quick-architecture diagram, sample traffic trace, QBR summary slide.

2) Technical Validation (days 7–21)
   - Deliverable: pilot plan + acceptance criteria (SLOs).
   - Activities: define pilot dataset/flows, capacity targets, latency/cost goals, access to staging infra or customer VPC. Run synthetic load or A/B routing to dedicated instance.
   - Measure: token throughput, P95 latency delta, per-token cost estimate post-quantization/batching.

3) Pilot Execution (weeks 3–6)
   - Deliverable: pilot report with metrics, customer sign-off (yes/no), risk remediation plan.
   - Activities: setup dedicated pool or private deployment (mini-scope), enable monitoring/tracing, run customer traffic (shadow/prod-lite), review results with customer engineering.

4) Commercialization & Contracting (weeks 5–8+)
   - Deliverable: SOW/amendment, committed capacity schedule, SLA appendix.
   - Activities: present pricing scenarios (committed vs burst), SLA tiers (standard/premium/enterprise), finalize billing start date and data controls.

5) Migration & Go-live (8–12 weeks)
   - Deliverable: migration runbook, cutover plan, rollback plan, post-migration monitoring dashboard.
   - Activities: pre-cutover validation, DNS/endpoint switch, smoke tests, hypercare (48–72h).

6) Post-sale enablement (ongoing)
   - Deliverable: playbook for cost-ops and efficiency reviews every 30/90 days.
   - Activities: tuning batch sizes, KV caching policies, quantization recommendations, cost allocation tags.

Packaging options (example bands — local guideline):
- Dedicated Starter: reserved capacity + basic support (SLA 99.5%). Good for mid-market customers with steady workloads. Typical commit: 2–8 GPUs/mo.
- Dedicated Plus: reserved + burst + 24x7 support + 99.9% SLA. Typical commit: 8–32 GPUs/mo.
- Private Core: private control plane, VPC peering, KMS integration, enterprise SLAs (99.95%), audit logging retention. Typical for regulated customers.
- Premium SLA Add-on: response time guarantees, dedicated on-call post-sale, increased observability retention.
Note: include example monthly price multipliers vs hosted baseline when discussing with commercial — we provide a templated price delta calculator to RevOps.

Playbook tactics & persuasion levers (engineer-first):
- Run a 48–72h 'latency needle' test that isolates a key customer flow and demonstrates P95 improvement on Dedicated.
- Provide a model-compatibility checklist and a tiny migration script to reduce SE effort.
- Offer a limited-time pilot credit for infra hours to offset migration validation costs.
- Share anonymized before/after economics from a similar tenant (percent cost reduction or latency improvement).

Sample outreach (technical thread) — short: 
Subject: "Proposal: 2-week Dedicated pilot to validate latency & cost for X flow"
Hi <Engineer>,
We propose a 2-week dedicated pilot scoped to your Search API flow (example traffic attached). Goal: validate P95 < 120ms and projected token-cost reduction ~25%. We’ll handle provision, monitoring, and a short runbook to revert if needed. Can you share a staging endpoint and a contact for test data?
Thanks,
<Nina / Solutions Eng>

Sample executive QBR ask (email):
Subject: "QBR item: capacity & SLA proposal to support growth"
Hi <Customer Exec>,
In your QBR we’d like to discuss an engineered capacity plan to support expected usage growth and options for a 99.9% SLA. This reduces outage risk and stabilizes unit economics. We’ll present a short pilot plan and a commercial outline. Are you available next week for a 20-minute slot?

Objection handling (brief matrix):
- "Too expensive" -> show committed-price per-token and 12-month cost projection vs hosted trend + migration credit.
- "We can self-host" -> highlight operational effort, monitoring coverage, and Redwood runbook + support delta.
- "Compliance" -> outline private deployment controls (KMS, audit logs, VPC) and sample SOC/ISO artifacts.

Risk mitigation & escalation path:
- If pilot fails to meet acceptance: pause migration, root-cause session within 3 business days, corrective action plan within 7 days.
- Escalation: CS lead -> SE -> Product lead -> Customer Success Director. Include on-call contact for critical SLA failures.

Metrics to track post-migration (monthly cadence):
- Net Revenue Retention impact from upgrade
- Committed vs actual GPU utilization
- P95 latency, error rate, deployment rollback count
- Cost per 1M effective tokens (post-optimization)
- Customer satisfaction (CSAT/NPS for migration)

Checklists (copyable):
- Pre-discovery: collect billing export, model list, token distribution, busiest endpoints
- Pre-pilot: define test flows, acceptance criteria, grant access to staging, baseline metrics captured
- Pre-contract: confirm legal SLA terms, commit amount, start date, payment terms
- Pre-cutover: finalize DNS, certs, run smoke tests, notify stakeholders

Example timeline (typical mid-market):
Weeks 0–1: discovery
Weeks 2–4: technical validation + pilot setup
Weeks 5–7: pilot run + performance review
Weeks 6–9: contracting concurrently
Week 10: migration & go-live

Next steps (CSM owner to run this checklist):
1) Kickoff meeting with customer engineering + SE within 5 business days
2) Create pilot plan doc and share acceptance criteria (owner: SE)
3) Open renewal/migration tracker row and notify RevOps

Appendix: quick references
- Technical artifacts to request: sample trace, model config, max sequence length, KV cache settings, current concurrency limits
- Internal playbook links: pricing calculator, legal SLA templates, Private deployment checklist

Notes and open questions (working):
- Evaluate introducing a short self-service "mini-dedicated" SKU for 2–4 GPU monthly commits to de-risk migration for smaller tenants.
- Experiment with a 30-day post-go-live cost optimization review as a standard deliverable.

End of document."
